The archive.org full-text index finds the line in the scan of The Private Life (privatelifepoems0000muel, LSU 1976): 'It is the singular gift / we cannot destroy in ourselves, / the argument that refutes death, ...'. It finds the same in Alive Together (1996), Good Poems and Traditions in Literature (1985/1987). The Yale Review for Autumn 1976 quotes the lines in its review of the book, and Roberts' Literature dates the poem 1976. Line count from the Alive Together OCR: stanza 1 has 8 lines. Stanza 2 has 8 lines, including 'it is the motion that runs / from the eyes to the tail of a dog,' and ending 'of the child that has just been born.' The New Millennium Reader puts its 15 at 'it is the mouth that inflates the lungs', so the third stanza runs 17 to 21. Roberts appears one line off, but its margin numbers sit between lines in the OCR, which is ambiguous rather than contrary. The quotation is the whole third stanza and ends at 'all we know of God.' The word God is in a secular poem, not scripture. shipped.js is clean: Mueller 0 of 3, not banned. The source is 94 characters.
